$comment: Spinr MCP server scaffold. NONE of these are wired to live credentials — every value below is a placeholder or an ${ENV_VAR} reference. Fill in env vars locally (never commit real secrets here) before a server will actually connect. See per-server notes for the specific sandboxing rule each one requires before use against Spinr.

stripe.$comment: OAuth-based, hosted by Stripe. Run `claude mcp add --transport http stripe https://mcp.stripe.com` and complete the browser login yourself. ONLY ever authenticate against a Stripe TEST-MODE account for this project — never the live Spinr Stripe account. This talks directly to routes/payments.py, wallet, and corporate billing flows.

sentry.$comment: OAuth-based, hosted by Sentry. Run `claude mcp add --transport http sentry https://mcp.sentry.dev` and complete the browser login to your Sentry org. Read-mostly (issues/traces/breadcrumbs). Scrub PII before pasting any stack trace into chat — raw GPS/phone/email/name are banned from Sentry payloads per CLAUDE.md and must not be re-introduced via chat.

redis.$comment: Requires REDIS_URL. MUST point at a staging/read-only Redis instance — never Spinr's live redis.spinr.ca. A write-capable Redis MCP against production could corrupt live dispatch state (spinr:ws:dispatch pub/sub) or rate-limit/OTP-lockout counters.

twilio.$comment: Requires Twilio Account SID + Auth Token. MUST be scoped to Twilio test credentials / test phone numbers only. A Twilio MCP with live creds can send real SMS to real riders/drivers and burn real OTP-lockout state.

google-maps.$comment: Community-maintained (not an official Google/Anthropic server) — re-verify maintenance activity before trusting it with a real billed API key. Requires its own Google Maps API key with a spend cap set, separate from the rider-app/backend production key.

firebase.$comment: Requires a Firebase service account JSON scoped to a single Spinr project, NOT the org-wide account used by backend/core/lifespan.py. Broad scope (Auth users, Storage) — restrict to least privilege before pointing at anything beyond a dev/staging Firebase project.

context7.$comment: Upstash, open-source (MIT), read-only doc lookup — no Spinr credentials, no write access, nothing to sandbox. Fetches current version-specific docs/examples for a library (e.g. Next.js App Router, Tailwind v4, Supabase JS) so responses don't rely on stale training data. Works with no API key at low rate limits; optionally set CONTEXT7_API_KEY (from context7.com/dashboard) for a higher limit.

chrome-devtools.$comment: Google, official (googlechrome/chrome-devtools-mcp). Launches its OWN Chrome instance (headless by default) and drives it via the Chrome DevTools Protocol — no Spinr credentials, but it CAN navigate to and interact with any URL the agent points it at, so treat it like any other browser: only point it at admin-dashboard's localhost dev server or public, non-authenticated pages, never paste real rider/driver session cookies or tokens into a page it opens. Useful for admin-dashboard debugging (console/network inspection, perf traces) and for authoring/triaging Playwright specs.
